target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## Summary

Session-backed managed worktrees are now leased for the lifetime of every agent run. Idle GC waits for an admitted run to finish before it can snapshot or force-remove that checkout, including when the run uses a subdirectory inside the worktree.

## Root cause

GC's owner-activity read and `git worktree remove --force` were independent operations. The previous patch repeated the read closer to removal, but a session could still be admitted after that read and while the destructive command started.

## Fix

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease. `agent-command` acquires the lease before a session run touches its configured cwd and releases it in its outer cleanup. All managed removal paths acquire the same lease through snapshotting and git removal; idle GC retains the owner-active guard after it has obtained that lease.

Lease lookup accepts a managed worktree root or one of its subdirectories, matching session worktrees whose configured workspace is nested below the repository root.

## Why this is the right boundary

The worktree service owns the destructive operation and is the only place that can serialize it consistently with its consumers. Agent command is the session-run admission point that has the resolved cwd and can retain the lease through the actual runtime. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics, while an agent that loses the race before admission fails before using a deleted cwd rather than running against it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: 24 passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts`, and `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Structured local review: no accepted or actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session must not have its managed checkout removed while its agent run is using that checkout or a nested workspace within it.
Real environment tested: pristine main `6eb9a5ada23b20353da9ef8e9fe69881567ca74f` and this patch `8a5ea1bac785439394ba6959fca805fa4231aee7`, driving the production ManagedWorktreeService against real on-disk git worktrees and filesystem state.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a session-owned worktree, start a lease from a nested directory, begin idle removal, confirm the directory remains present while the lease is held, release the lease, then observe the same queued removal complete.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6eb9a5a)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: false
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: false
# AFTER (this patch 8a5ea1b)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: true
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: true
```
Observed result after fix: a live session retains its nested working directory until its lease ends, after which queued cleanup can complete normally.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the production worktree lifecycle and real git filesystem operations were exercised in-process.
